However, that 98% efficiency is the energy from the combustible gases produced versus the energy of the DC pulses. It is not 98% of the energy put in to the system to produce the pulses. So a non-negligible amount of energy is lost in producing the pulses, but the energy of the pulses themselves was 98% efficient in disassociating the water molecules.

98% efficiency is pretty damn good in the energy conversion world, especially for someone who had no formal background in physics (I think he was a farmer or something), though his brother, who did seem to have a background in electronics, collaborated with him.

Interestingly, it seems he was not running an electric current through the water. That is, this was not brute-force electrolysis. He was using the water as the dielectric in a capacitor and the dc pulses to vary the voltage of that capacitor to perform the splitting.
